title: Carpets, soft furnishings, walls and blinds
audience: Cleaning staff who clean carpets, upholstered items and wall or window coverings in healthcare areas.
learningOutcomes: Describe the routine vacuuming and periodic cleaning method for carpets in patient areas.
State the method for cleaning a spill on soft furnishings.
Explain when walls and blinds are cleaned.

instruction.heading: Carpets
instruction.body: Carpets in lobbies and general patient zones get a daily vacuum run by a machine whose filter traps very fine particles, so dust does not drift back out. Deep cleaning happens on the schedule the facility sets, using a technique that throws up little mist and leaves little film.

instruction.heading: Soft furnishings
instruction.body: Upholstery that has been spilled on gets a detergent mix, never hypochlorite. Wet extraction is another option. Once treated, open up the room as much as you can so the piece is fully dry before anyone sits on it.

instruction.heading: Walls and blinds
instruction.body: Patient-room walls and blinds get a detergent wipe-down once dust or grime appears. Window curtains are replaced on a fixed cycle, and they go to the laundry early if they pick up soil or have been near a multi-resistant organism.

instruction.heading: Why the method matters
instruction.body: The guideline asks for carpet cleaning that produces little spray and leaves little residue, and it warns against the wrong chemical on upholstery. For soft furnishings the drying time is part of the method, not an optional extra.

procedure: Vacuum the carpets in the assigned area using a HEPA-filtered vacuum, as facility policy requires.
For a carpet spill, first remove the solid matter as far as possible, then use the facility's extraction method.
For a soft furnishing spill, apply detergent mix with a cloth, then wipe it clean.
Wet vacuum a soft furnishing where the facility method allows it.
Ventilate the room until the furnishing is dry before reuse.
Log the method and the date for each periodic clean.

workedExamples.situation: A visitor spills a cup of tea on an upholstered visitor chair in a patient room. The chair is not a clinical item.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which method is right, and which product is off limits?
workedExamples.reasoning: Clean it with a detergent mix, then ventilate the room so the chair dries before reuse. Do not use hypochlorite on the upholstery, because the guideline advises against it for soft furnishings.

equipmentAndPpe: HEPA-filtered vacuum or wet vacuum, as the area allows

commonErrors.error: Using a disinfectant on upholstery because it looks dirty.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a detergent mix. Check the label before using any other product.

commonErrors.error: Leaving upholstery damp because the room is busy.
commonErrors.prevention: Ventilate the room so the item dries before reuse.

commonErrors.error: Using a dry vacuum with a standard filter on carpets.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a HEPA-filtered vacuum where the policy requires it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Ventilate the room while surfaces dry, and mark wet floors so people do not slip.
Carpet machines and cleaning chemicals must follow the maker's directions and the facility's approved method.

qualityStandard: Carpets are vacuumed on the scheduled days with the stated filter.
Soft furnishings are dry before reuse.
Walls and blinds are washed when they look soiled, and each job is logged.
documentationEvidence: Carpet and periodic clean record with date and method
Record of a soft furnishing spill cleaned, with the drying time
summary: Patient-area carpets are vacuumed daily with HEPA-filtered equipment.
Soft furnishings are cleaned with detergent, not hypochlorite, and dried before reuse.
Walls and blinds are cleaned with detergent when visibly soiled.

knowledgeChecks.question: What type of vacuum filter does the guideline recommend for patient-area carpets?
options: No filter at all and no bag fitted
A filter that traps very fine particles.
A paper bag only, and nothing else
A filter chosen by the cleaner each day.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which response suits a spill on an upholstered item?
options: A hypochlorite solution applied and left overnight.
A detergent mix, then ventilation until dry.
Alcohol, applied and left to evaporate.
A dry cloth rubbed over the stain.

knowledgeChecks.question: When does a patient-room wall or blind need a detergent wash?
options: Only when the room is painted
Once a week, as a fixed rule.
When they look dusty or dirty.
Only by the end of the year

sourceReferences: Australian Guidelines for Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare, B1.4.2 (carpet, walls, blinds and curtains); B1.4.3 (soft furnishings); rights: not held by user; reworded (no copying)
